paras: The Moultrie depot whipping was the beating of an unnamed Black railroad employee by two white men outside Moultrie, Georgia, on the night of Saturday, 29 August 1903. Freed on bond after being accused of kicking a white depot clerk, the man was marched beyond the city limits and, by report, whipped with a buggy trace; he was not seen again in the town.

That Saturday night, while the Atlantic and Birmingham train from Fitzgerald stood at the Moultrie depot, a Black employee of the road quarreled with Walter LeGrave, a young boy who clerked at the depot. According to the Moultrie correspondent, the employee kicked LeGrave in the face "without any warning," leaving him unconscious. The train's conductor started toward the employee but was stopped by Marshal Cason, and later that evening the man gave bond and was released.

As he walked down the street after his release, two white men came up on either side of him and ordered him to "keep walking," accompanying him past the city limits. The correspondent called what happened next "mere conjecture," but reported that "a buggy trace in the hands of a strong man" had played a part in "the punishment." The man had not been seen since, which the dispatch explained by saying he was "not able to walk."

The names of the two white men could not be learned, the dispatch said, because they were said to be strangers in the city. No report of an arrest, inquiry or further news of the beaten man appears in the coverage.

The only account found ran in the Fitzgerald Enterprise, a weekly in the town the train had come from, on 8 September 1903 under a Moultrie dateline of 1 September. Its headline, "Whipped an Insolent Negro," and subhead, "'Strangers' at Moultrie Cause a Mild Sensation over Unruly Black," presented the beating as deserved punishment. The dispatch called the victim "a big strapping fellow" who had kicked a boy and named none of his attackers.
No coverage of the episode was found in the Black press or in other white papers.

accounts.label: Moultrie correspondent
accounts.gist: The employee kicked the clerk 'without any warning', gave bond, and was walked out of town by two white strangers; what followed is 'mere conjecture', but a buggy trace reportedly 'played an important part in the punishment' and he has not been seen.

framing.detail: Headlined 'Whipped an Insolent Negro' and 'Mild Sensation over Unruly Black'; calls the beating 'the punishment', puts 'Strangers' in quotation marks, and presents the kick as unprovoked.
